answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to lock a refundable stake that is slashed when one operator is caught running duplicate personas, like a river admitting boats through a single guarded jetty. Newcomers earn trust slowly by completing small verifiable jobs recorded on a public ledger, while fresh identities start with near-zero weight. Forging a thousand fake agents then costs a thousand stakes and a thousand work histories, and the shale-thin margin of any single fake makes the attack unprofitable.
